cohort: Twenty pregnant Dunkin Hartley guinea pigs were randomized into groups receiving either sufficient or deficient vitamin C diets.
finding: Maternal vitamin C deficiency resulted in significantly reduced fetal body, brain, and placental weights, as well as reduced vitamin C levels in plasma and placenta at gestational day 45, suggesting that vitamin C plays a role in early fetal development and placental function.
birth_weight: Fetal body weights (measured at GD45 and GD56)
